metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: The LORD’s word that came to Micah of Morasheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
units.rightText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah the Moreshite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah — what he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem:
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: Hear, you peoples, all of you! Listen, O earth, and all that is therein. Let the Lord GOD be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
units.rightText: Hear, O peoples, all of you; listen, O earth, and everyone in it! May the Lord GOD bear witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.

units.leftText: For behold, the LORD comes out of his place, and will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
units.rightText: For behold, the LORD comes forth from His dwelling place; He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
leftNotes: 1:3 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: The mountains melt under him, and the valleys split apart like wax before the fire, like waters that are poured down a steep place.
units.rightText: The mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.

units.leftText: “All this is for the disobedience of Jacob, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the disobedience of Jacob? Isn’t it Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Aren’t they Jerusalem?
units.rightText: All this is for the transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?

units.leftText: Therefore I will make Samaria like a rubble heap of the field, like places for planting vineyards; and I will pour down its stones into the valley, and I will uncover its foundations.
units.rightText: Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting area for a vineyard. I will pour her stones into the valley and expose her foundations.

units.leftText: All her idols will be beaten to pieces, all her temple gifts will be burned with fire, and I will destroy all her images; for of the hire of a prostitute has she gathered them, and to the hire of a prostitute shall they return.”
units.rightText: All her carved images will be smashed to pieces; all her wages will be burned in the fire, and I will destroy all her idols. Since she collected the wages of a prostitute, they will be used again on a prostitute. Weeping and Mourning

units.leftText: For this I will lament and wail. I will go stripped and naked. I will howl like the jackals and mourn like the ostriches.
units.rightText: Because of this I will lament and wail; I will walk barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich.
rightNotes: 1:8 Or a serpent or a dragon
1:8 Literally like daughters of an ostrich or like daughters of an owl

units.leftText: For her wounds are incurable; for it has come even to Judah. It reaches to the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For her wound is incurable; it has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself.

units.leftText: Don’t tell it in Gath. Don’t weep at all. At Beth Ophrah I have rolled myself in the dust.
units.rightText: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. Roll in the dust in Beth-leaphrah.
leftNotes: 1:10 Beth Ophrah means literally “House of Dust.”
rightNotes: 1:10 Gath sounds like the Hebrew for tell.
1:10 Beth-leaphrah means house of dust.

units.leftText: Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame. The inhabitant of Zaanan won’t come out. The wailing of Beth Ezel will take from you his protection.
units.rightText: Depart in shameful nakedness, O dwellers of Shaphir. The dwellers of Zaanan will not come out. Beth-ezel is in mourning; its support is taken from you.
rightNotes: 1:11 Shaphir means pleasant.
1:11 Zaanan sounds like the Hebrew for come out.
1:11 Beth-ezel means adjoining house.

units.leftText: For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good, because evil has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For the dwellers of Maroth pined for good, but calamity came down from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem.
rightNotes: 1:12 Maroth sounds like the Hebrew for bitter.

units.leftText: Harness the chariot to the swift steed, inhabitant of Lachish. She was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion; for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
units.rightText: Harness your chariot horses, O dweller of Lachish. You were the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
rightNotes: 1:13 Lachish sounds like the Hebrew term for team of horses.

units.leftText: Therefore you will give a parting gift to Moresheth Gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deceitful thing to the kings of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore, send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib will prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.
rightNotes: 1:14 Or give dowry
1:14 Moresheth sounds like the Hebrew for gift or dowry.
1:14 Achzib means deception.

units.leftText: I will yet bring a conqueror to you, inhabitants of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
units.rightText: I will again bring a conqueror against you, O dweller of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
rightNotes: 1:15 Mareshah sounds like the Hebrew for conqueror.

units.leftText: Shave your heads, and cut off your hair for the children of your delight. Enlarge your baldness like the vulture, for they have gone into captivity from you!
units.rightText: Shave yourselves bald and cut off your hair in mourning for your precious children; make yourselves as bald as an eagle, for they will go from you into exile.

units.leftText: Woe to those who devise iniquity and work evil on their beds! When the morning is light, they practice it, because it is in the power of their hand.
units.rightText: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil on their beds! At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.

units.leftText: They covet fields and seize them, and houses, then take them away. They oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.
units.rightText: They covet fields and seize them; they take away houses. They deprive a man of his home, a fellow man of his inheritance.

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD says: “Behold, I am planning against these people a disaster, from which you will not remove your necks, neither will you walk haughtily, for it is an evil time.
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “I am planning against this nation a disaster from which you cannot free your necks. Then you will not walk so proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.

units.leftText: In that day they will take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, saying, ‘We are utterly ruined! My people’s possession is divided up. Indeed he takes it from me and assigns our fields to traitors!’”
units.rightText: In that day they will take up a proverb against you and taunt you with this bitter lamentation: ‘We are utterly ruined! He has changed the portion of my people. How He has removed it from me! He has allotted our fields to traitors.’”

units.leftText: Therefore you will have no one who divides the land by lot in the LORD’s assembly.
units.rightText: Therefore, you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot. Reproof of False Prophets (Ezekiel 13:1–16|EZK 13:1-16*)

units.leftText: “Don’t prophesy!”—they prophesy— “Don’t prophesy about these things. Disgrace won’t overtake us.”
units.rightText: “Do not preach,” they preach. “Do not preach these things; disgrace will not overtake us.”

units.leftText: Shall it be said, O house of Jacob, “Is the LORD’s Spirit angry? Are these his doings? Don’t my words do good to him who walks blamelessly?”
units.rightText: Should it be said, O house of Jacob, “Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these the things He does?” Do not My words bring good to him who walks uprightly?

units.leftText: But lately my people have risen up as an enemy. You strip the robe and clothing from those who pass by without a care, returning from battle.
units.rightText: But of late My people have risen up like an enemy: You strip off the splendid robe from unsuspecting passersby like men returning from battle.

units.leftText: You drive the women of my people out from their pleasant houses; from their young children you take away my blessing forever.
units.rightText: You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes. You take away My blessing from their children forever.

units.leftText: Arise, and depart! For this is not your resting place, because of uncleanness that destroys, even with a grievous destruction.
units.rightText: Arise and depart, for this is not your place of rest, because its defilement brings destruction— a grievous destruction!

units.leftText: If a man walking in a spirit of falsehood lies, saying, “I will prophesy to you of wine and of strong drink,” he would be the prophet of this people.
units.rightText: If a man of wind were to come and say falsely, “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be just the preacher for this people! The Remnant of Israel (Micah 5:7–15|MIC 5:7-15*)
rightNotes: 2:11 Or “I will prophesy to you for wine and strong drink”

units.leftText: I will surely assemble all of you, Jacob. I will surely gather the remnant of Israel. I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as a flock in the middle of their pasture. They will swarm with people.
units.rightText: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the midst of its pasture — a noisy throng.

units.leftText: He who breaks open the way goes up before them. They break through the gate, and go out. Their king passes on before them, with the LORD at their head.
units.rightText: One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate, and go out by it. Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader.

units.leftText: I said, “Please listen, you heads of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel: Isn’t it for you to know justice?
units.rightText: Then I said: “Hear now, O leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel. Should you not know justice?

units.leftText: You who hate the good, and love the evil; who tear off their skin, and their flesh from off their bones;
units.rightText: You hate good and love evil. You tear the skin from my people and strip the flesh from their bones.

units.leftText: who also eat the flesh of my people, and peel their skin from off them, and break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as meat within the cauldron.
units.rightText: You eat the flesh of my people after stripping off their skin and breaking their bones. You chop them up like flesh for the cooking pot, like meat in a cauldron.”

units.leftText: Then they will cry to the LORD, but he will not answer them. Yes, he will hide his face from them at that time, because they made their deeds evil.”
units.rightText: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them. At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done.

units.leftText: The LORD says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray—for those who feed their teeth, they proclaim, “Peace!” and whoever doesn’t provide for their mouths, they prepare war against him:
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “As for the prophets who lead My people astray, who proclaim peace while they chew with their teeth, but declare war against one who puts nothing in their mouths:

units.leftText: “Therefore night is over you, with no vision, and it is dark to you, that you may not divine; and the sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will be black over them.
units.rightText: Therefore night will come over you without visions, and darkness without divination. The sun will set on these prophets, and the daylight will turn black over them.

units.leftText: The seers shall be disappointed, and the diviners confounded. Yes, they shall all cover their lips, for there is no answer from God.”
units.rightText: Then the seers will be ashamed and the diviners will be disgraced. They will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God.”

units.leftText: But as for me, I am full of power by the LORD’s Spirit, and of judgment, and of might, to declare to Jacob his disobedience, and to Israel his sin.
units.rightText: As for me, however, I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.

units.leftText: Please listen to this, you heads of the house of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel, who abhor justice, and pervert all equity,
units.rightText: Now hear this, O leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and pervert all that is right,

units.leftText: who build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
units.rightText: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity.

units.leftText: Her leaders judge for bribes, and her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money; yet they lean on the LORD, and say, “Isn’t the LORD among us? No disaster will come on us.”
units.rightText: Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD, saying, “Is not the LORD among us? No disaster can come upon us.”

units.leftText: Therefore Zion for your sake will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps of rubble, and the mountain of the temple like the high places of a forest.
units.rightText: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a wooded ridge.

units.leftText: But in the latter days, it will happen that the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be established on the top of the mountains, and it will be exalted above the hills; and peoples will stream to it.
units.rightText: In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and the peoples will stream to it.

units.leftText: Many nations will go and say, “Come! Let’s go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law will go out of Zion, and the LORD’s word from Jerusalem;
units.rightText: And many nations will come and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths.” For the law will go forth from Zion and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

units.leftText: and he will judge between many peoples, and will decide concerning strong nations afar off. They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, neither will they learn war any more.
units.rightText: Then He will judge between many peoples and arbitrate for strong nations far and wide. Then they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor will they train anymore for war.

units.leftText: But every man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree. No one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.
units.rightText: And each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to frighten him. For the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.

units.leftText: Indeed all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
units.rightText: Though all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, yet we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever. The Restoration of Zion (Zechariah 8:1–23|ZEC 8:1-23*)

units.leftText: “In that day,” says the LORD, “I will assemble that which is lame, and I will gather that which is driven away, and that which I have afflicted;
units.rightText: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast, even those whom I have afflicted.

units.leftText: and I will make that which was lame a remnant, and that which was cast far off a strong nation: and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from then on, even forever.”
units.rightText: And I will make the lame into a remnant, the outcast into a strong nation. Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever.

units.leftText: You, tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come. Yes, the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And you, O watchtower of the flock, O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion — the former dominion will be restored to you; sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem.”
rightNotes: 4:8 Or hill; Hebrew And you, Migdal-eder, the Ophel

units.leftText: Now why do you cry out aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pains have taken hold of you as of a woman in travail?
units.rightText: Why do you now cry aloud? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor perished so that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?

units.leftText: Be in pain, and labor to give birth, daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail; for now you will go out of the city, and will dwell in the field, and will come even to Babylon. There you will be rescued. There the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
units.rightText: Writhe in agony, O Daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor. For now you will leave the city and camp in the open fields. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies!

units.leftText: Now many nations have assembled against you, that say, “Let her be defiled, and let our eye gloat over Zion.”
units.rightText: But now many nations have assembled against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let us feast our eyes on Zion.”

units.leftText: But they don’t know the thoughts of the LORD, neither do they understand his counsel; for he has gathered them like the sheaves to the threshing floor.
units.rightText: But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His plan, for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

units.leftText: Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron, and I will make your hoofs bronze. You will beat in pieces many peoples. I will devote their gain to the LORD, and their substance to the Lord of the whole earth.
units.rightText: Rise and thresh, O Daughter of Zion, for I will give you horns of iron and hooves of bronze to break to pieces many peoples. Then you will devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
rightNotes: 4:13 Or devote to destruction

units.leftText: Now you shall gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops. He has laid siege against us. They will strike the judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek.
units.rightText: Now, O daughter of troops, mobilize your troops; for a siege is laid against us! With a rod they will strike the cheek of the judge of Israel.

units.leftText: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me who is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings out are from of old, from ancient times.
units.rightText: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel — One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity.
rightNotes: 5:2 Or thousands
5:2 Cited in Matthew 2:6|MAT 2:6*

units.leftText: Therefore he will abandon them until the time that she who is in labor gives birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor has given birth; then the rest of His brothers will return to the children of Israel.

units.leftText: He shall stand, and shall shepherd in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. They will live, for then he will be great to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: He will stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majestic name of the LORD His God. And they will dwell securely, for then His greatness will extend to the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and when he marches through our fortresses, then we will raise against him seven shepherds, and eight leaders of men.
units.rightText: And He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and tramples our citadels. We will raise against it seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men.
rightNotes: 5:5 Or their peace

units.leftText: They will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its gates. He will deliver us from the Assyrian, when he invades our land, and when he marches within our border.
units.rightText: And they will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with the blade drawn. So He will deliver us when Assyria invades our land and marches into our borders. The Remnant of Jacob (Micah 2:12–13|MIC 2:12-13*)

units.leftText: The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, that don’t wait for man nor wait for the sons of men.
units.rightText: Then the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for man or linger for mankind.

units.leftText: The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep; who, if he goes through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to deliver.
units.rightText: Then the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it passes through, with no one to rescue them.

units.leftText: Let your hand be lifted up above your adversaries, and let all of your enemies be cut off.
units.rightText: Your hand will be lifted over your foes, and all your enemies will be cut off.

units.leftText: “It will happen in that day”, says the LORD, “that I will cut off your horses from among you and will destroy your chariots.
units.rightText: “In that day,” declares the LORD, “I will remove your horses from among you and wreck your chariots.

units.leftText: I will cut off the cities of your land and will tear down all your strongholds.
units.rightText: I will remove the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.

units.leftText: I will destroy witchcraft from your hand. You shall have no soothsayers.
units.rightText: I will cut the sorceries from your hand, and you will have no fortune-tellers.

units.leftText: I will cut off your engraved images and your pillars from among you; and you shall no more worship the work of your hands.
units.rightText: I will also cut off the carved images and sacred pillars from among you, so that you will no longer bow down to the work of your own hands.

units.leftText: I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you; and I will destroy your cities.
units.rightText: I will root out the Asherah poles from your midst and demolish your cities.

units.leftText: I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath on the nations that didn’t listen.”
units.rightText: I will take vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that have not obeyed Me.”

units.leftText: Listen now to what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear what you have to say.
units.rightText: Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.

units.leftText: Hear, you mountains, the LORD’s indictment, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a case against his people, and he will contend with Israel.
units.rightText: Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment, you enduring foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel:

units.leftText: My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me!
units.rightText: ‘My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!

units.leftText: For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage. I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
units.rightText: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam.

units.leftText: My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD.”
units.rightText: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD.’”
rightNotes: 6:5 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: How shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
units.rightText: With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?

units.leftText: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams? With tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my disobedience? The fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
units.rightText: Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

units.leftText: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
units.rightText: He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God? The Punishment of Israel

units.leftText: The LORD’s voice calls to the city— and wisdom fears your name— “Listen to the rod, and he who appointed it.
units.rightText: The voice of the LORD calls out to the city (and it is sound wisdom to fear Your name): “Heed the rod and the One who ordained it.

units.leftText: Are there yet treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and a short ephah that is accursed?
units.rightText: Can I forget any longer, O house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness and the short ephah, which is accursed?
leftNotes: 6:10 An ephah is a measure of volume (about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel), and a short ephah is made smaller than a full ephah for the purpose of cheating customers.

units.leftText: Shall I tolerate dishonest scales, and a bag of deceitful weights?
units.rightText: Can I excuse dishonest scales or bags of false weights?

units.leftText: Her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their speech.
units.rightText: For the wealthy of the city are full of violence, and its residents speak lies; their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.

units.leftText: Therefore I also have struck you with a grievous wound. I have made you desolate because of your sins.
units.rightText: Therefore I am striking you severely, to ruin you because of your sins.

units.leftText: You shall eat, but not be satisfied. Your hunger will be within you. You will store up, but not save, and that which you save I will give up to the sword.
units.rightText: You will eat but not be satisfied, and your hunger will remain with you. What you acquire, you will not preserve; and what you save, I will give to the sword.

units.leftText: You will sow, but won’t reap. You will tread the olives, but won’t anoint yourself with oil; and crush grapes, but won’t drink the wine.
units.rightText: You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink the wine.

units.leftText: For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of Ahab’s house. You walk in their counsels, that I may make you a ruin, and your inhabitants a hissing. You will bear the reproach of my people.”
units.rightText: You have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of Ahab’s house; you have followed their counsel. Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of contempt; you will bear the scorn of the nations. ”
rightNotes: 6:16 LXX; Hebrew scorn of My people

units.leftText: Misery is mine! Indeed, I am like one who gathers the summer fruits, as gleanings of the vineyard. There is no cluster of grapes to eat. My soul desires to eat the early fig.
units.rightText: Woe is me! For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.

units.leftText: The godly man has perished out of the earth, and there is no one upright among men. They all lie in wait for blood; every man hunts his brother with a net.
units.rightText: The godly man has perished from the earth; there is no one upright among men. They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net.

units.leftText: Their hands are on that which is evil to do it diligently. The ruler and judge ask for a bribe. The powerful man dictates the evil desire of his soul. Thus they conspire together.
units.rightText: Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.

units.leftText: The best of them is like a brier. The most upright is worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, even your visitation, has come; now is the time of their confusion.
units.rightText: The best of them is like a brier; the most upright is sharper than a hedge of thorns. The day for your watchmen has come, the day of your visitation. Now is the time of their confusion.
rightNotes: 7:4 Or your punishment

units.leftText: Don’t trust in a neighbor. Don’t put confidence in a friend. With the woman lying in your embrace, be careful of the words of your mouth!
units.rightText: Do not rely on a friend; do not trust in a companion. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
rightNotes: 7:5 Hebrew in your bosom

units.leftText: For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.
units.rightText: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies are the members of his own household. Israel’s Confession and Comfort
rightNotes: 7:6 Cited in Matthew 10:35–36|MAT 10:35-36*; see also Luke 12:53.

units.leftText: But as for me, I will look to the LORD. I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
units.rightText: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.

units.leftText: Don’t rejoice against me, my enemy. When I fall, I will arise. When I sit in darkness, the LORD will be a light to me.
units.rightText: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.

units.leftText: I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and executes judgment for me. He will bring me out to the light. I will see his righteousness.
units.rightText: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.

units.leftText: Then my enemy will see it, and shame will cover her who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her. Now she will be trodden down like the mire of the streets.
units.rightText: Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame — she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.

units.leftText: A day to build your walls! In that day, he will extend your boundary.
units.rightText: The day for rebuilding your walls will come — the day for extending your boundary.

units.leftText: In that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt even to the River, and from sea to sea, and mountain to mountain.
units.rightText: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, even from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
rightNotes: 7:12 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Yet the land will be desolate because of those who dwell therein, for the fruit of their doings.
units.rightText: Then the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds. God’s Compassion on Israel

units.leftText: Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your heritage, who dwell by themselves in a forest. Let them feed in the middle of fertile pasture land, in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
units.rightText: Shepherd with Your staff Your people, the flock of Your inheritance. They live alone in a woodland, surrounded by pastures. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
rightNotes: 7:14 Or in a woodland, in the midst of Carmel

units.leftText: “As in the days of your coming out of the land of Egypt, I will show them marvelous things.”
units.rightText: As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders.

units.leftText: The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They will lay their hand on their mouth. Their ears will be deaf.
units.rightText: Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.

units.leftText: They will lick the dust like a serpent. Like crawling things of the earth, they will come trembling out of their dens. They will come with fear to the LORD our God, and will be afraid because of you.
units.rightText: They will lick the dust like a snake, like reptiles slithering on the ground. They will come trembling from their strongholds in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You.

units.leftText: Who is a God like you, who pardons iniquity, and passes over the disobedience of the remnant of his heritage? He doesn’t retain his anger forever, because he delights in loving kindness.
units.rightText: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance — who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
rightNotes: 7:18 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
units.rightText: He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities. You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea.

units.leftText: You will give truth to Jacob, and mercy to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.
units.rightText: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
